description: Submitting the exact same result payload twice for the same attempt (e.g. an HTTP retry after a dropped response) succeeds idempotently and returns the original accepted result, with no duplicate side effects.
notes: The Backend already implements exactly this (GameAttempt.Complete / VersusSeries.CompleteAttempt: a second Complete call with the same attempt is a silent no-op returning the original result; GameRound is not re-resolved). Unity's Attempt.Complete does NOT special-case this: it throws VersusDomainException on ANY second completion, identical or not (see fixture 11's notes). This is the one place a naive parity check would wrongly conclude 'incompatible' - they only agree because retries never reach Unity's local domain a second time in the correspondence flow (the coordinator's own request already succeeded locally before it was ever sent), whereas the Backend must tolerate a second HTTP delivery of a request whose first delivery it already applied. See issue #8 section 13: 'semantically identical' is a protocol-level (transport-retry) concern, not a claim that both domains contain the same guard.
